leads.title: Gambia Criminal Code (1933), Section 158
leads.documents: Colonial-era criminalisation of same-sex sexual conduct as 'carnal knowledge against the order of nature'; punishable by up to 14 years imprisonment for both men and women
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Section 158 of the Criminal Code, punishable by up to 14 years imprisonment' - implemented 1934, remained in force

leads.title: Criminal Code (Amendment) Act, 2005
leads.documents: Amendment criminalising sexual behavior between women as 'gross indecency', extending criminalisation to women
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Criminal Code (Amendment) Act, 2005' amending Section 158 to include women

leads.title: Criminal Code (Amendment) Act 2014
leads.documents: Introduced crime of 'aggravated homosexuality' for serial offenders, people living with HIV, acts with minors under 18, disabled/drugged persons, parent/guardian/authority figure; mandatory life sentence; signed Oct 2014 by President Jammeh
leads.detail: Cited as 'Criminal Code (Amendment) Act 2014' introducing 'aggravated homosexuality' with life imprisonment

leads.title: Gambia Criminal Code, Section 167
leads.documents: Restricts transgender gender expression - forbids men to dress 'as women'; cross-dressing punishable by up to 5 years jail or 50,000 Gambian dalasi fine; in force since 2013
leads.detail: Cited as 'section 167 of the Criminal Code, which forbids men to dress "as women"'

leads.title: Gambia Criminal Code Section 147(1) - Brusubi Magistrates' Court ruling, March 2026
leads.documents: Enforcement example: Muhammad Jawo and Muhammad Krubally each sentenced to five years imprisonment for sexual activity in unfinished building; Magistrate Isatou Jallow guilty verdict for indecent conduct between men
leads.detail: Cited as 'Magistrate Isatou Jallow of the Brusubi Magistrates' Court declared them guilty of violating Section 147(1)'

leads.title: U.S. Department of State Human Rights Reports - 2011 Human Rights Report
leads.documents: Reports laws against homosexual activity are rarely enforced; strong societal discrimination against LGBTQ individuals, some shunned; no reported physical violence against LGBTQ individuals during 2011; privacy, HIV healthcare, employment discrimination context
leads.detail: Cited as 'U.S. Department of State's 2011 Human Rights Report' and 'United States Department of State reports that the laws...are rarely enforced'

leads.title: Human Rights Watch
leads.documents: NGO reporting that Gambian law enforcement carries out regular organised actions against persons suspected of homosexuality and gender non-conformity, contradicting rare-enforcement claim
leads.detail: Cited as 'the NGO Human Rights Watch reports regular organised actions by law enforcement against persons suspected of homosexuality and gender non-conformity'

leads.title: Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission (TRRC)
leads.documents: Government rights machinery attempting impartial record of human rights abuses under Jammeh presidency; notes lack of data on gay arrests and safety concerns preventing LGBT+ Gambians testifying
leads.detail: Cited with deputy executive secretary Musu Bakoto Sawo quote: 'a high probability of victims not coming out'.

leads.title: The Point - 'TRRC witness calls for inclusion of gay, lesbian rights in new constitution'
leads.documents: Documents TRRC testimony calling for gay/lesbian rights inclusion in new constitution; rights reform effort post-Jammeh
leads.detail: Further reading citation: 'The Point staff (22 January 2020). "TRRC witness calls for inclusion of gay, lesbian rights in new constitution". The Point. Retrieved 14 November 2022.'

leads.title: SBS News - 'Politicians push to scrap Gambia's harsh anti-gay legislation'
leads.documents: Documents post-2017 political push to scrap harsh anti-gay legislation under President Adama Barrow government
leads.detail: Further reading citation: 'Morgan, Michaela (19 May 2017). "Politicians push to scrap Gambia's harsh anti-gay legislation". SBS News. Retrieved 14 November 2022.'
